name: Cefepime
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Cefepime is cleared mainly by the kidneys, and its clearance falls in proportion to creatinine clearance (CrCl). The US label keeps the first dose unchanged and reduces maintenance doses when CrCl is 60 mL/min or less, with set regimens for hemodialysis and CAPD. Unadjusted doses in kidney impairment cause neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures, nonconvulsive status epilepticus).
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl (mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault); adjust at 60 or less.

bands.recommendation: CrCl >60: usual dose (label: 500 mg to 2 g every 8 to 12 hours by indication). CrCl of exactly 60: use the 30–60 row.
CrCl 30–60, by usual regimen: 500 mg q12h → 500 mg q24h; 1 g q12h → 1 g q24h; 2 g q12h → 2 g q24h; 2 g q8h → 2 g q12h. First dose as for normal function (label Table 2).
bands.short: Same dose q24h (2 g q8h → q12h)

bands.recommendation: CrCl 11–29, by usual regimen: 500 mg q12h → 500 mg q24h; 1 g q12h → 500 mg q24h; 2 g q12h → 1 g q24h; 2 g q8h → 2 g q24h (label Table 2).
CrCl 11–14: as the 11–29 row. CrCl below 11, by usual regimen: 250 mg, 250 mg, 500 mg or 1 g every 24 hours respectively (label Table 2).

hd.text: 1 g on day 1, then 500 mg every 24 hours; for the 2 g every 8 hours regimen (febrile neutropenia) 1 g every 24 hours; give at the same time each day and after hemodialysis on dialysis days (label). A 3-hour session removes about 68% of the drug in the body. Literature option (not label): thrice-weekly after each session, 2 g, 2 g and 2 g (1/1/1.5 g and 1.5/1.5/2 g reported in limited data) (Tsai 2025). Troughs of 22 mg/L or more have been associated with neurotoxicity; stop if encephalopathy or myoclonus appears. These regimens are not weight-adjusted and come mostly from small pharmacokinetic studies; confirm the actual last and next session before each dose. See the site guide Antibiotic Stewardship in Hemodialysis (/guides/antibiotic-stewardship-dialysis.html).
hd.short: 1 g, then 500 mg q24h, after HD

pd.text: CAPD: the usual dose every 48 hours (500 mg, 1 g, 2 g or 2 g by regimen) (label Table 2). For PD-associated peritonitis (ISPD 2022): intraperitoneal intermittent 1,000 mg daily; continuous loading dose 500 mg/L, then 125 mg/L in each exchange. Continuous cephalosporin doses may need about 25% more in patients with significant residual kidney function (ISPD 2022).
pd.short: CAPD: usual dose q48h; IP per ISPD

crrt.text: Not in label. Li 2020 (Table 3): CVVH ultrafiltration 1,000 mL/h or less, 1 g every 8 hours; 1,500 mL/h or more, 2 g every 8 hours or 1 g every 6 hours; 30 mL/kg/h, 2 g every 8 hours as extended infusion. CVVHD dialysate 20–25 mL/kg/h, load 2 g, then 1.5–1.75 g every 8 hours. CVVHDF combined flow 1,000 mL/h or less, 1 g every 8 hours; 1,500 mL/h or more, 2 g every 8 hours or 1 g every 6 hours.

dialyzable: Yes: about 68% removed during a 3-hour hemodialysis (label). For overdose the label advises hemodialysis, not peritoneal dialysis. Protein binding about 20%.
monitoring: CrCl for dose; neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures, nonconvulsive status epilepticus), mainly with unadjusted doses in kidney impairment; stop cefepime if it occurs (label 5.2). Kidney function with aminoglycosides or loop diuretics.

pediatric.usual_dose: Up to 40 kg: 50 mg/kg every 12 hours (every 8 hours for febrile neutropenia and P. aeruginosa pneumonia) (label).
pediatric.max_dose: Not above the recommended adult dose (label).
